PTX L1 prefetch hints (2 iterations ahead) + vectorized bf16 output writes — neutral impact, absolute latencies similar to baseline, speedup variance from Modal reference timing

8-warp blocks (256 threads) extended to B>2 — doubles warps/SM for medium batches
8-warp blocks (256 threads) extended to B>4 — targets medium batches (B=5-16 with sf=2, rows_per_warp=8)

8-row register pipeline for rows_per_warp>=16 (B>=5): 16 interleaved warp reductions for maximum ILP — regression in speedup (-23.2%), but absolute latency improved 13% (0.016ms vs 0.0184ms), likely Modal reference variance + register pressure

ld.global.cg for state loads -- bypass L1 (65.6% throughput bottleneck), cache in L2 only for cross-invocation residency — neutral impact (0.018ms vs 0.0184ms baseline), speedup regression from Modal reference variance

TMA cp.async.bulk double-buffer pipeline for B>16 -- shared memory staging via DMA engine. CRITICAL FAILURE: 22/54 workloads crashed with XID 13 (SM Global Exception / Multiple Warp Errors) causing GPU context corruption. First crash on workload a8c8beff (TIMEOUT), cascading to all subsequent workloads (18 RUNTIME_ERROR). Likely out-of-bounds memory access in large-batch kernel path.

TMA cp.async.bulk per-row 512B copies (fix attempt for entry #29) — ALL 11 workloads TIMEOUT, GPU unresponsive. cp.async.bulk+mbarrier fundamentally incompatible with TVM FFI build environment (likely PTX arch mismatch). Both attempts reverted.
8-row pipeline with enable_smem_spilling pragma + __launch_bounds__(256,4) for B>16 — regression: mean -23.4%, max -36%, smem spill latency + reduced prefetch overlap outweighed ILP gains

3-stage cp.async.ca shared memory pipeline (replaces register-based 4-row prefetch for num_iter>=3, i.e., B>4). Register path retained for B<=4 (num_iter<=2). 24KB/48KB dynamic smem per block. RESULT: 32/54 workloads PASSED, 22/54 RUNTIME_ERROR on the larger-batch workloads that exercise the new smem pipeline path. Small-batch workloads (old register path) still pass cleanly. Stats computed over 32 passing only. Bug in the shared memory pipeline path - likely out-of-bounds smem access, missing cp.async commit/wait barrier, or wrong stage indexing.

3-stage cp.async.ca smem pipeline v2: fixed 2 bugs from v1 (added cudaFuncSetAttribute for >48KB smem, changed 3-ahead to 2-ahead prefetch to avoid RAW hazard). B>4 uses cp.async pipeline, B<=4 uses register path.
Streaming stores (st.global.cs.v4.f32) for new_state writes — skip write-allocate under cold-L2 framework. Absolute latency 0.01682ms vs fresh baseline 0.01197ms (+40% slower). Reverted.
Baseline re-measurement under current framework (post .cs revert) — same kernel as entry #19 from 2026-04-08
sm_100a compilation verification via TVM_FFI_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=10.0a env var in Modal Image — same kernel code, different nvcc arch flag

Fused output vector: w=q-qk_dot*beta*k, output=scale*(g*ws+qk_dot_beta*v) — decouples output from residual dependency chain. Neutral impact (0.01509ms within Modal variance range 0.012-0.017ms of baseline)

TMA cp.async.bulk double-buffer smem pipeline for B>16 (separate gdn_decode_kernel_tma, 32KB dynamic smem, mbarrier sync). B<=16 unchanged (register path). KEY FINDING: TMA works on sm_100a without crashes (entries #29-30 crashed on sm_100). Performance neutral/slightly worse: B>16 mean latency 0.019ms (smem read penalty ~28 cycles × 16 reads = 448 cycles/iter). Better than entry #33 cp.async.ca (-21%), confirming TMA DMA engine increases BIF, but smem penalty still limits.

FULL MODE baseline (warmup=3, iterations=100, trials=5) of current register-based kernel after TMA revert. Per-batch latency: B=1 0.0112ms, B=4 0.0113ms, B=8 0.012ms, B=16 0.013ms, B=32 0.014ms, B=48 0.016ms, B=64 0.0185ms. Very low within-batch variance confirms full mode is the reliable measurement. This supersedes quick-mode entry #35 as the authoritative baseline.

sf=2 for B>16 (was sf=1): 1024 vs 512 blocks at B=64, intended to improve tail utilization on 148-SM B200. RESULT: net regression on absolute latency. Per-batch: B=48 +6.2%, B=64 +8.1%. Theoretical 'tail utilization' analysis was flawed — blocks don't execute in discrete waves; each SM does same total work regardless of sf (block_count × rows_per_block fixed). Added overhead from 2x block scheduling overhead + duplicate v smem loads. Mean speedup metric misleadingly high (1622x vs 1465x) due to Modal reference run-to-run variance.

Full mode + use_isolated_runner=True on current baseline kernel (post sf=2 revert). Absolute latency 0.01354ms matches non-isolated baseline 0.01361ms (within noise). Mean speedup 1578x differs from non-isolated 1465x because isolated runner affects reference timing. Per-batch: B=1 11.4us, B=4 11.25us, B=8 12us, B=16 12.43us, B=32 14us, B=48 16.14us, B=64 18.13us. Confirms kernel performance is stable across runner modes — absolute latency is the reliable cross-run metric, not speedup ratio.
